subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the standard electronic systems model, which three stages are used to describe how a system works?
questions.explain: Electronic systems are analysed using the input-process-output model.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation LDR stand for?
questions.explain: An LDR is a light dependent resistor whose resistance changes with light level.

questions.q: What happens to the resistance of an LDR as the light falling on it increases?
questions.explain: As light intensity rises, the LDR's resistance falls.

questions.q: Which physical quantity does a thermistor sense?
questions.explain: A thermistor is a temperature-dependent resistor used to sense heat.

questions.q: In a common NTC thermistor, what happens to its resistance as the temperature rises?
questions.explain: A negative temperature coefficient (NTC) thermistor's resistance falls as temperature rises.

questions.q: Which of the following is an output device in an electronic system?
questions.explain: An LED is an output device that converts electrical energy into light.

questions.q: Why is a resistor placed in series with an LED in a circuit?
options: To limit the current and protect the LED
To make the LED brighter than normal
To store charge for the LED
questions.explain: A series (current-limiting) resistor keeps the LED current safe to prevent damage.

questions.q: A microcontroller is best described as which type of component?
questions.explain: A microcontroller is a programmable component whose behaviour is set by code.

questions.q: What is a key advantage of using a microcontroller instead of many separate components?
options: It can be reprogrammed and reduces the number of components needed
It removes the need for any power supply
It cannot be changed once built, improving safety
It only works with mechanical inputs
questions.explain: Microcontrollers reduce component count and can be reprogrammed to change function.

questions.q: Which sensor is commonly used to detect the movement of a person by sensing infrared?
questions.explain: A passive infrared (PIR) sensor detects movement from the infrared given off by a body.

questions.q: What is the role of the process stage in an electronic system?
options: To make a decision or perform an operation on the input signal
To directly generate light or sound
To supply mains power to the circuit
questions.explain: The process stage acts on input signals to decide what the output should do.

questions.q: A designer wants a garden light to switch on automatically when it gets dark. Which input sensor is most suitable?
questions.explain: An LDR detects the fall in light level so the lamp can turn on at dusk.

questions.q: A greenhouse needs an alarm that triggers when the temperature drops too low. Which input sensor should be used?
questions.explain: A thermistor senses temperature change so a low-temperature alarm can respond.

questions.q: Which of these is an output device that produces sound?
questions.explain: A buzzer is an output device that converts electrical energy into sound.

questions.q: In many control circuits, what is a transistor most often used to do?
questions.explain: A transistor is commonly used as a fast, electronic switch to turn outputs on and off.

questions.q: Which method is commonly used to plan and write a program for a microcontroller in GCSE D&T?
questions.explain: Flowcharts are commonly used to plan and produce the program for a microcontroller.

questions.q: An automatic shop door should open when a customer approaches. Which input device is most appropriate?
questions.explain: A PIR sensor detects the customer's movement so the door can open automatically.

questions.q: Why might a relay be used in a control circuit?
options: To let a small current switch a separate larger current or higher voltage load
To reduce the resistance of the whole circuit
To sense the level of light in a room
To store the program for the system
questions.explain: A relay uses a small control current to switch a much larger or higher-voltage load safely.

questions.q: A resistor has 4V across it and a current of 0.02A flowing through it. Using V = IR, what is its resistance?
Why is flash memory useful in a microcontroller used for prototyping?
options: It can be erased and reprogrammed many times
It permanently fixes the program at manufacture
It replaces the need for any input sensors
questions.explain: Flash memory lets the microcontroller be reprogrammed repeatedly, ideal for testing designs.
